title: Continuous Auctions and Insider Trading
supported_mechanism_claims: Trading can transmit private information into prices through a dynamic price-impact process.
Market depth is a core state variable linking order flow to price response.
scope_note: Used only as public theory background; no BTCUSDT or project outcome result is imported.

title: Bid, Ask and Transaction Prices in a Specialist Market with Heterogeneously Informed Traders
supported_mechanism_claims: Trades can convey information when market participants face adverse selection.
Bid-ask spreads and realizable prices matter when translating observed price changes into executable economics.
scope_note: Used as mechanism background for information-bearing flow and execution-aware interpretation.

title: Measuring the Information Content of Stock Trades
supported_mechanism_claims: The information effect of trades can arrive with a lag rather than instantaneously.
Trade impact can depend on trade size and prevailing spread/liquidity conditions.
scope_note: Qualitative public evidence only; no numerical findings are copied into R1 idea packets.

title: How Markets Slowly Digest Changes in Supply and Demand
supported_mechanism_claims: Order flow can be persistent because large parent orders are executed incrementally.
Liquidity can adapt dynamically to persistent order flow, so impact is not a fixed mechanical response.
scope_note: Used to motivate persistence-versus-adaptive-liquidity mechanisms without importing project outcomes.

title: The Price Impact of Order Book Events
supported_mechanism_claims: Short-horizon price response can be linked to order-flow imbalance at the best quotes.
Price response to imbalance can vary inversely with available market depth.
scope_note: Used as public mechanism evidence; R1.1 does not assume the relationship transfers unchanged to BTCUSDT.

title: Optimal Trading Strategy and Supply/Demand Dynamics
supported_mechanism_claims: Liquidity is dynamic; resilience describes how supply and demand recover after a trade.
The speed of liquidity recovery can matter separately from static spread and depth.
scope_note: Used to motivate fast-versus-slow liquidity recovery as a state, not to choose any threshold or horizon.

title: Limit Order Books
supported_mechanism_claims: Limit-order-book dynamics expose multiple interacting dimensions of liquidity rather than a single static depth measure.
Empirical LOB regularities and model assumptions should not be treated as universally transferable without validation.
scope_note: Used as broad background and as a caution against over-interpreting one book statistic.

title: Queue Imbalance as a One-Tick-Ahead Price Predictor in a Limit Order Book
supported_mechanism_claims: Near-touch bid-versus-ask queue imbalance can contain information about the direction of the next mid-price movement.
Queue pressure is a candidate immediate-state variable rather than a complete trading proposition by itself.
scope_note: Used qualitatively; R1.1 does not import fitted coefficients or significance values.

title: No-Dynamic-Arbitrage and Market Impact
supported_mechanism_claims: The shape of market impact and the way impact decays through time are jointly constrained.
Transient-versus-persistent impact should be treated as a dynamic process rather than a fixed one-shot effect.
scope_note: Used to motivate impact-decay families without assuming a particular parametric decay function.

title: Trading and Arbitrage in Cryptocurrency Markets
supported_mechanism_claims: Cryptocurrency markets can exhibit economically meaningful cross-exchange price deviations.
Common and venue-specific signed-volume components can carry different information about aggregate returns and cross-venue dislocations.
scope_note: Used only to justify cross-venue information-diffusion hypotheses as a legitimate family; no paper statistic is used as a project result.
